security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives caused by ordinary JWT, HTTP error-handling, React context, and testing terminology. SKILL.md is conceptual guidance and contains no executable instructions for reconnaissance, data collection, or harmful activity.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line lists a valid JWT as required authorization input for an API client. It does not instruct the user to discover systems, credentials, or services.

content.user_title: Build a JWT-Aware Next.js API Client
content.value_statement: Next.js applications need consistent authorization, token refresh, and API error handling. This skill provides a design framework for a centralized JWT-aware client.
actual_capabilities: Defines a centralized API communication layer for Next.js applications.
Explains how to attach JWT bearer tokens to authorized requests.
Outlines token expiry detection and coordinated refresh behavior.
Describes consistent handling for authentication and API errors.
Covers client-side and server-side integration considerations.
Lists testing areas for token, refresh, and concurrent-request behavior.
limitations: Provides conceptual guidance rather than production-ready source code.
Does not implement a specific authentication provider or backend endpoint.
Does not choose a token storage method for the application.
Requires developers to apply the guidance to their security and deployment requirements.

use_cases.title: Standardize a growing frontend
use_cases.description: Create shared API client conventions across routes and components.

use_cases.title: Plan JWT refresh behavior
use_cases.description: Define safe handling for expired tokens and concurrent requests.

use_cases.title: Review API integration design
use_cases.description: Check request, response, error, and testing responsibilities before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start an API client plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a centralized Next.js API client that attaches a JWT bearer token and handles HTTP errors.

prompt_templates.title: Define token refresh flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a token expiry and refresh flow for my Next.js API client. Include refresh failure behavior and login redirection.

prompt_templates.title: Separate browser and server logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to separate JWT API client behavior between Next.js client components and server components.

prompt_templates.title: Review concurrent request handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my API client design for concurrent requests during token refresh. Identify coordination, retry, and error-handling requirements.

output_examples.input: Plan a JWT API client for a Next.js application.
output: A centralized request interface with typed request options.
Bearer token attachment for protected endpoints.
A refresh workflow that redirects after refresh failure.

output_examples.input: What should I test in the token refresh flow?
output: Multiple requests arriving during a single refresh.
Refresh failure, cleanup, and login redirection.

best_practices: Use HTTPS for every authenticated API request.
Keep authorization, refresh, and error logic in one tested client layer.
Avoid exposing tokens or sensitive server details in client-facing errors.
anti_patterns: Do not duplicate token attachment logic across individual components.
Do not retry refresh requests indefinitely after authentication failures.
Do not store or log sensitive token values without a reviewed security decision.

faq.question: Does this skill provide ready-to-run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides a conceptual implementation framework.

faq.question: Is this limited to Next.js?
faq.answer: The guidance focuses on Next.js, but several API client patterns apply to other React applications.

faq.question: Does it select a token storage method?
faq.answer: No. Token storage must match the application security model.

faq.question: Does it support token refresh?
faq.answer: It explains refresh requirements, failure handling, and request coordination.

faq.question: Can it handle server-side API calls?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies separate server-side and client-side integration considerations.

faq.question: What should I test first?
faq.answer: Test token attachment, expiration, refresh failure, and concurrent request behavior.
